7765.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
7765.question_text: Which of the following BEST describes Abraham's reaction of God's promise of a son by Sarah?
7765.explanation:
Abraham’s reaction to God's promise of a son by Sarah is best described as faithfulness because he believed in God’s word despite his old age and Sarah's barrenness.

In Genesis 15:6 (RSV), it is written:
"And he believed the Lord; and he reckoned it to him as righteousness."

This verse shows that Abraham trusted God’s promise completely, even though it seemed impossible from a human perspective. His faith was later reaffirmed in Romans 4:20-21 (RSV):
"No distrust made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God, fully convinced that God was able to do what he had promised."

7811.question_text: When the Pharisees accused Jesus disciples of plucking heads of grain on the Sabbath, Jesus referred them to what David did during the high priesthood of
7811.explanation: In Mark 2:25-26 and Luke 6:3-4, Jesus referred to an incident involving David during the high priesthood of Abiathar when responding to the Pharisees' accusation about his disciples plucking heads of grain on the Sabbath. This reference highlights Jesus' point about the legitimacy of actions taken out of necessity or mercy even if they seem to violate strict Sabbath rules.

7812.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
7812.question_text: 'Take head and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees'. This leaven is their
7812.explanation:
In Matthew 16:6, 12 (RSV), Jesus warns His disciples:

"Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees."

Later, in Matthew 16:12, it is clarified:

"Then they understood that he did not tell them to beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees."

Here, "leaven" is used metaphorically to represent the false doctrines and misleading teachings of the Pharisees and Sadducees, which could corrupt true faith.
